answer: Give every identity a narrow inlet: a single service endpoint whose capacity is proven live, not claimed. Peers probe it through a prism of independent checks — latency, throughput, and completed jobs — and publish a violet-tinted trust score that fades unless refreshed by real work. A Sybil swarm must then rent or run a real endpoint per fake, each costing bandwidth and upkeep, while copied or idle endpoints score zero and lose trading rights.
